newsitem.title: USA: Chronology of Paula Jones lawsuit against Clinton.
newsitem.headline: Chronology of Paula Jones lawsuit against Clinton.

text.p: Following is a chronology of events surrounding the sexual harassment lawsuit filed by Paula Jones against President Bill Clinton:

December 1993 -- American Spectator publishes allegation that Arkansas state troopers arranged secret liaisons for then-Arkansas Governor Clinton with several women, including one referred to only as "Paula."

Feb. 11, 1994 -- Jones appears at a news conference in Washington saying Clinton had asked her for "a type of sex" when the two were alone in an Arkansas hotel room on May 8, 1991. She was an Arkansas state employee at the time.
May 6, 1994 -- Jones' lawyers, Gilbert Davis and Joseph Cammarata, file the lawsuit seeking $700,000 in compensatory and punitive damages.

Oct. 7, 1994 -- Jones appears at Hollywood news conference to read a statement to reporters about failed negotiations between her attorneys and Clinton's lawyers. She says she is sorry Clinton did not accept her settlement offer and that she only wants restoration of her good name.
Dec. 28, 1994 -- A federal judge in Arkansas, Susan Webber Wright, delays the suit, ruling that it would not go to trial until Clinton is out of office. Jones' lawyers appeal.
Jan. 9, 1996 -- A federal appeals court in St. Louis says the case can go ahead while Clinton is in office. Clinton's lawyer, Robert Bennett, appeals.

May 27, 1997 -- A unanimous Supreme Court rules that Jones's sexual harassment lawsuit against Clinton can proceed immediately rather than wait until he leaves office, sending the case back to the federal judge in Arkansas for more hearings. Davis predicts a trial would start "within a year."
